subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 45-year-old man reports that his urine darkens after standing and that he has chronic low back and knee pain. Examination shows bluish-gray pigmentation of the ear cartilage and sclerae. Urine organic acid analysis shows a large amount of homogentisic acid.
question: Deficiency of which enzyme is the most likely cause?
explanation_correct: Homogentisate oxidase deficiency blocks tyrosine degradation, so homogentisic acid accumulates and polymerizes into a dark pigment that deposits in cartilage and connective tissue, producing ochronosis. This causes early arthropathy, bluish-gray discoloration of cartilage and sclerae, and urine that darkens on standing.

explanation_incorrect.A: Phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency causes phenylketonuria, not ochronosis.
explanation_incorrect.B: Tyrosinase deficiency causes albinism; it does not cause homogentisic acid accumulation.
explanation_incorrect.C: Tyrosine aminotransferase deficiency is a cause of tyrosinemia and does not cause ochronosis.
explanation_incorrect.E: Fumarylacetoacetate hydrolase deficiency causes tyrosinemia type I, with hepatic failure and renal tubular dysfunction rather than ochronosis.

educationalObjective: Homogentisate oxidase deficiency causes alkaptonuria, with homogentisic acid accumulation, ochronosis, dark urine, and arthropathy.
